name: engine-guide
description: Building on Godot 4 (C# or GDScript), Bevy, Babylon.js, three.js or HTML: which to choose, installing its toolchain, the project sketch, build commands, headless capture to screenshots and video, and the traps that fail silently. Use when starting or working on a game, a video made in an engine (presentation, explainer, trailer, product showcase), an interactive 3D or 2D page, or anything else built on one of these engines.

findings.excerpt: - macOS has no `timeout`, which the Godot guide wraps every call in: `brew install coreutils` provides it as `gtimeout`.
The current stable is the newest release on GitHub: `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/godotengine/godot/releases/latest` gives the tag (`X.Y.Z-stable`) and
- **macOS:** `brew install --cask godot-mono` for C#; the plain `godot` cask's command runs without C#. Make `godot` on `PATH` a wrapper script, not a symlink —
- **.NET SDK for C#:** the newest one (`dotnet-install.sh` from dot.net into `~/.dotnet`, with `DOTNET_ROOT` set and it on `PATH`; `brew install dotnet` on macO
